name: Uncharted
scope: Drake tetralogy plus The Lost Legacy. Golden Abyss (Vita) and the Fight for Fortune spin-offs are out of scope.
caveat: Present-day chronology matches release order. The flashbacks in Uncharted 3 (young Drake in Cartagena) and Uncharted 4 (the orphanage, Panama) are the earliest events in the series, but they sit inside games that come later, so the games stay in this order. Play order and chronology agree here.

games.title: Uncharted: Drake’s Fortune
games.note: Never released on PC. Sold only inside The Nathan Drake Collection (2015), which runs the three PS3 games at 1080p/60.

editions.name: Uncharted: Drake's Fortune
editions.note: Original release; stuck on PS3 hardware.

editions.name: Uncharted: The Nathan Drake Collection
editions.note: Bluepoint remaster at 1080p/60; only modern way to play it.

games.title: Uncharted 2: Among Thieves
games.note: Still the high point of the series. Collection only; no PC release has ever happened.

editions.name: Uncharted 2: Among Thieves
editions.note: Original release; PS3 only.

editions.name: Uncharted 2: Among Thieves - Game of the Year Edition
editions.note: Adds multiplayer map and skin DLC; single-player story unchanged.

editions.name: Uncharted: The Nathan Drake Collection
editions.note: Remastered 1080p/60 campaign; best and only current-gen version.

games.title: Uncharted 3: Drake’s Deception
games.note: Chronology: opens on the earliest material in the franchise — a teenage Drake in Cartagena — but the present-day thread follows Uncharted 2 directly.

editions.name: Uncharted 3: Drake's Deception
editions.note: Original release; PS3 only.

editions.name: Uncharted 3: Drake's Deception - Game of the Year Edition
editions.note: Bundles multiplayer DLC; campaign identical to launch.

editions.name: Uncharted: The Nathan Drake Collection
editions.note: Remastered campaign at 1080p/60; multiplayer dropped.

games.title: Uncharted 4: A Thief’s End
games.note: On PC via the Legacy of Thieves Collection — a solid port. The MSRP covers this and Lost Legacy together. Multiplayer is cut from the PC version.

editions.name: Uncharted 4: A Thief's End
editions.note: Original release; 30fps on base PS4.

editions.name: Uncharted: Legacy of Thieves Collection
editions.note: Remaster of 4 plus Lost Legacy; 60/120fps and the only PC version.

games.title: Uncharted: The Lost Legacy
games.note: Chloe and Nadine, set shortly after Uncharted 4. Bundled into Legacy of Thieves, never sold alone. Skippable without losing the Drake story.

editions.name: Uncharted: The Lost Legacy
editions.note: Original standalone release.

editions.name: Uncharted: Legacy of Thieves Collection
editions.note: Remastered and paired with Uncharted 4; adds PC and 60/120fps modes.

name: Assassin’s Creed
scope: Mainline only. No Chronicles, no mobile entries, no Liberation or Freedom Cry standalones.
caveat: This is the tab where chronology and play order pull hardest in opposite directions. Rows are sorted by historical setting. The modern-day frame — Desmond across AC1–III, Layla across Origins–Valhalla — runs in release order and is a continuous story of its own. Recommended play order is therefore release order: AC1 → II → Brotherhood → Revelations → III → Black Flag → Rogue → Unity → Syndicate → Origins → Odyssey → Valhalla → Mirage → Shadows.

games.title: Assassin’s Creed Odyssey
games.note: 431 BCE, Peloponnesian War. Earliest setting in the series. Its modern-day half belongs to the Layla arc that starts in Origins — play it after. MSRP is the standard edition; Ultimate bundles the expansions.

editions.name: Assassin's Creed Odyssey
editions.note: Base game; both story arcs sold separately.

editions.name: Assassin's Creed Odyssey Gold Edition
editions.note: Adds Legacy of the First Blade and The Fate of Atlantis arcs.

editions.name: Assassin's Creed Odyssey Ultimate Edition
editions.note: Gold plus a cosmetic pack; no extra story over Gold.

games.title: Assassin’s Creed Origins
games.note: 49–43 BCE Egypt. Founding of the Hidden Ones and the start of the Layla modern-day arc.

editions.name: Assassin's Creed Origins
editions.note: Base game only; both expansions sold separately.

editions.name: Assassin's Creed Origins Gold Edition
editions.note: Adds The Hidden Ones and The Curse of the Pharaohs expansions.

games.title: Assassin’s Creed Mirage
games.note: 861 CE Baghdad. Basim’s origin story — a prequel to Valhalla that lands far better if you play Valhalla first.

games.title: Assassin’s Creed Valhalla
games.note: 873 CE England. Longest game in the series by a wide margin and closes the Layla arc. MSRP is standard edition; the Complete Edition folds in the three expansions.

editions.name: Assassin's Creed Valhalla
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
editions.note: Base game only; every expansion sold separately.

editions.name: Assassin's Creed Valhalla Ragnarok Edition
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
editions.note: Base game plus Dawn of Ragnarok only.

editions.name: Assassin's Creed Valhalla Complete Edition
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
editions.note: All expansions plus The Last Chapter; full Eivor story in one buy.

games.title: Assassin’s Creed
games.note: 1191, Third Crusade. Repetitive by modern standards, but it opens the Desmond frame that AC III pays off.

editions.name: Assassin's Creed
editions.note: Original console release; fewer mission types.

editions.name: Assassin's Creed: Director's Cut Edition
editions.note: Adds extra investigation missions; the only version still sold.

games.title: Assassin’s Creed II
games.note: 1476–1499 Italy. The usual recommended entry point despite AC1 preceding it — its opening recaps enough. The Ezio Collection remaster is console-only; PC gets the 2009 build.

editions.name: Assassin's Creed II
editions.note: Original release; missing story sequences 12 and 13.

editions.name: Assassin's Creed II: Game of the Year Edition
editions.note: Adds Battle of Forli and Bonfire of the Vanities story DLC.

editions.name: Assassin's Creed: The Ezio Collection
editions.note: Remastered with all story DLC; playable today, no multiplayer.

games.title: Assassin’s Creed Brotherhood
games.note: 1499–1507 Rome. Direct continuation of AC II, same protagonist, no gap.

editions.name: Assassin's Creed Brotherhood
editions.note: Original release, DLC sold separately.

editions.name: Assassin's Creed Brotherhood: Complete Edition
editions.note: Bundles The Da Vinci Disappearance and bonus content.

editions.name: Assassin's Creed: The Ezio Collection
editions.note: Remastered with all single-player DLC included.

games.title: Assassin’s Creed Revelations
games.note: 1511 Constantinople. Closes out Ezio and Altaïr both.

editions.name: Assassin's Creed Revelations
editions.note: Original release; The Lost Archive sold separately.

editions.name: Assassin's Creed Revelations Gold Edition
editions.note: Base game plus The Lost Archive and bonus packs.

editions.name: Assassin's Creed: The Ezio Collection
editions.note: Remastered, includes The Lost Archive and the Ezio short films.

games.title: Assassin’s Creed Shadows
games.note: 1579 Japan. Close to self-contained; its links to the wider story are light.

editions.name: Assassin's Creed Shadows
editions.note: Base game; the Claws of Awaji expansion is not included.

editions.name: Assassin's Creed Shadows Gold Edition
editions.note: Includes the expansion pass with the Claws of Awaji story chapter.

games.title: Assassin’s Creed IV: Black Flag
games.version: Assassin's Creed IV: Black Flag Gold Edition
games.note: 1715–1722 Caribbean. Best-liked entry and a fine standalone, but Edward’s story is a side branch. Its modern-day sections are set at Abstergo, after AC III.

editions.name: Assassin's Creed IV: Black Flag
editions.platforms: PS3 / PS4 / Xbox 360 / Xbox One / PC
editions.note: Original release; Freedom Cry sold separately.

editions.name: Assassin's Creed IV: Black Flag Gold Edition

editions.name: Assassin's Creed: The Rebel Collection
editions.note: Black Flag plus Rogue with DLC; portable but lower fidelity.

authored.version: Assassin's Creed IV: Black Flag Gold Edition

games.title: Assassin’s Creed Rogue
games.note: 1752–1760 North Atlantic. Bridges Black Flag to AC III from the Templar side. The 2018 Remastered edition is console-only; PC has the 2015 original.

editions.name: Assassin's Creed Rogue
editions.note: Original last-gen release.

editions.name: Assassin's Creed Rogue
editions.note: PC port carrying the console special-edition bonus missions.

editions.name: Assassin's Creed Rogue Remastered
editions.note: 4K remaster with all bonus missions; best-looking version.

editions.name: Assassin's Creed: The Rebel Collection
editions.note: Rogue plus Black Flag with DLC; portable but lower fidelity.

games.title: Assassin’s Creed III
games.note: 1754–1783 American Revolution. Ends the Desmond arc — the payoff for AC1 through Revelations. The 2019 Remaster changed lighting and character models and is divisive; the 2012 original is also on PC.

editions.name: Assassin's Creed III
editions.note: Original release; Tyranny of King Washington sold separately.

editions.name: Assassin's Creed III Remastered
editions.note: 4K remaster with all DLC plus Liberation Remastered bundled in.

games.title: Assassin’s Creed Unity
games.note: 1789 Paris. Disastrous launch, long since patched; now one of the better-looking entries in the series.

games.title: Assassin’s Creed Syndicate
games.note: 1868 London. The last game before the series turned into an RPG.

editions.name: Assassin's Creed Syndicate
editions.note: Base game; Jack the Ripper story DLC sold separately.

editions.name: Assassin's Creed Syndicate Gold Edition
editions.note: Season pass included: Jack the Ripper and The Last Maharaja stories.

name: Horizon
scope: Zero Dawn and Forbidden West, both expansions included. Lego Horizon Adventures and Call of the Mountain (VR) are out of scope.
caveat: Chronology and play order agree. Both expansions sit after their base game’s main story rather than alongside it.

games.title: Horizon Zero Dawn
games.note: The 2024 Remastered edition replaced the Complete Edition, which is now delisted on Steam. Existing owners were offered a paid upgrade rather than a free one.

editions.name: Horizon Zero Dawn
editions.note: Original release; The Frozen Wilds sold separately.

editions.name: Complete Edition
editions.note: Adds The Frozen Wilds expansion and bonus gear.

editions.name: Complete Edition (PC)

editions.name: Remastered
editions.note: Rebuilt visuals and Forbidden West systems, with The Frozen Wilds.

games.note: Bundled with the Remastered edition. Optional on paper, but it introduces hardware and characters Forbidden West assumes you have met.

editions.name: The Frozen Wilds
editions.note: Standalone expansion purchase; requires the base game.

editions.name: Horizon Zero Dawn Complete Edition
editions.note: Bundles the expansion with the base game; PC version in 2020.

editions.name: Horizon Zero Dawn Remastered
editions.note: Expansion included and rebuilt alongside the base game.

games.title: Horizon Forbidden West
games.note: The PC release (2024) is the Complete Edition and a good port. Picks up directly from Zero Dawn’s ending.

editions.name: Horizon Forbidden West
editions.note: Original release; Burning Shores was not yet out.

editions.name: Complete Edition

games.title: Horizon Forbidden West: Burning Shores
games.note: Bundled with the Complete Edition. Not optional in practice — its ending is the clearest setup for whatever comes third.

editions.name: Burning Shores
editions.note: Standalone expansion purchase; PS5 only, no PS4 version.

editions.name: Horizon Forbidden West Complete Edition
editions.note: Bundles the expansion with the base game; PC version followed in 2024.

name: Resident Evil
scope: Mainline numbered entries plus RE0, Code: Veronica, RE7 and Village. No Revelations, Outbreak, Umbrella Corps or spin-off shooters.
caveat: RE3 and RE2 overlap. Nemesis begins 28 September 1998, a day before RE2, and ends after it — so RE3 sorts first by chronological start. Recommended play order is the reverse: RE2 then RE3, because RE3 assumes you have already seen the Raccoon City outbreak from Leon and Claire’s side.

games.title: Resident Evil 0
games.note: 23 July 1998, hours before RE1. HD Remaster (2016) on PC. A prequel written long after the fact and the easiest mainline entry to drop.

editions.name: Resident Evil Zero
editions.note: Original release, GameCube exclusive.

editions.name: Wii port
editions.note: Straight port with Wii controls; no added content.

editions.name: HD Remaster
editions.note: HD rework plus optional modern controls and Wesker Mode.

games.title: Resident Evil
games.note: Play the 2002 GameCube remake, sold on PC as the HD Remaster (2015) — not the 1996 original. Tank controls are optional in this version.

editions.name: HD Remaster

games.title: Resident Evil 3
games.note: Starts a day before RE2 and ends after it. The 2020 remake cuts large parts of the 1999 original — the clock tower, the park, most of the Nemesis encounters. Six hours, and the one remake with a real asterisk.

editions.name: Resident Evil 3: Nemesis
editions.note: Original release; adds the live-selection choice system.

editions.name: GameCube port
editions.note: Straight port of the 1999 game.

editions.name: Resident Evil 3 (remake)

editions.name: Next-gen update
editions.note: Free upgrade to the remake; best-looking version of the story.

games.title: Resident Evil 2
games.note: 29 September 1998, mid-way through RE3’s timeline. The 2019 remake is the series benchmark. Two campaigns; the second run is a variant, not a sequel.

editions.name: Resident Evil 2
editions.note: Original two-disc release with the A/B scenario structure.

editions.name: GameCube port

editions.note: Original release; missing both story episodes.

editions.note: Free visual upgrade; content identical to Gold Edition.

games.title: Resident Evil Village
games.note: Direct sequel to RE7. The Gold Edition adds the Shadows of Rose epilogue, which later material builds on.

editions.note: Original release; ends before the Rose epilogue chapter.

editions.note: Bundles Winters' Expansion with the Shadows of Rose story DLC.

games.title: Resident Evil Requiem
games.note: Ninth mainline entry, released 27 February 2026. Returns to Raccoon City with a new protagonist. Runtime left blank — the figures are still settling.

name: Half-Life
scope: Mainline plus the two Gearbox expansions and Alyx. Black Mesa is a fan remake and is not counted here.
caveat: Alyx is the trap. It is set roughly five years before Half-Life 2, so it sorts here — but its final scene is a direct continuation of Episode Two’s cliffhanger and spoils it outright. Play it last. There is still no Half-Life 3 as of August 2026.

games.title: Half-Life
games.note: Holds up. Black Mesa (2020, sold separately) is a well-regarded fan remake if the 1998 visuals are a barrier — it is not official and is not counted in this tab.

editions.name: Half-Life
editions.note: Original retail release.

editions.name: Game of the Year Edition
editions.note: Same campaign plus Team Fortress Classic and extras.

editions.name: Half-Life: Source
editions.note: Source port with water and physics only; buggier than the original.

editions.name: 25th Anniversary Update
editions.note: Free Steam update: bundles Uplink, restores maps, adds widescreen.

games.title: Half-Life: Blue Shift
games.note: Runs in parallel with Half-Life from Barney Calhoun’s side. Three hours, low stakes — though Barney matters in HL2.

editions.name: Half-Life: Blue Shift

editions.name: Steam release

editions.name: Half-Life 1 Anthology
editions.note: Bundle with Half-Life, Opposing Force and Team Fortress Classic.

games.title: Half-Life: Opposing Force
games.note: Begins hours after the resonance cascade and ends after Gordon leaves Black Mesa. The stronger of the two expansions.

editions.name: Half-Life: Opposing Force
editions.note: Original retail expansion; requires Half-Life installed.

editions.name: Steam release
editions.note: Standalone on Steam; no anniversary update, but the maintained version.

editions.name: Half-Life 1 Anthology
editions.note: Bundle with Half-Life, Blue Shift and Team Fortress Classic.

games.note: Requires a VR headset — there is no flat-screen mode. Chronologically here, but play it after Episode Two or you spoil the single biggest moment in the series.

games.title: Half-Life 2
games.note: The 20th-anniversary build is the current version and now ships Episode One and Episode Two inside the base app.

editions.name: Half-Life 2
editions.note: Original release; ends on the Citadel cliffhanger.

editions.name: Half-Life 2: 20th Anniversary Update
editions.note: Folded into Half-Life 2 itself on Steam; no separate purchase.

editions.name: Half-Life 2: 20th Anniversary Update

name: Red Dead
scope: Red Dead Redemption 2 then Red Dead Redemption. Red Dead Revolver shares a name and nothing else.
caveat: Chronology and play order agree, and both run backwards from release order: RDR2 (1899) precedes RDR (1911). RDR2’s epilogue hands you straight to RDR’s opening situation.

games.title: Red Dead Redemption 2
games.note: 1899. Excellent PC version. The epilogue is effectively RDR1’s prologue — do not stop at the credits.

editions.name: Standard Edition
editions.note: Complete single-player story; the pricier editions add no story content.

editions.name: Special Edition
editions.note: Bank robbery mission and gameplay bonuses, not a real story expansion.

editions.name: Ultimate Edition
editions.note: Special Edition extras plus Online cosmetics and bonuses; no added story.

editions.name: Red Dead Redemption 2 (PC)
editions.note: Same story with extra bounties, weapons and photo mode; best fidelity.

games.title: Red Dead Redemption
games.note: 1911. The 2024 PC release is a port of the 2023 console conversion, not a remaster — 4K and uncapped frame rate over 2010 assets, and widely criticised for the price. Undead Nightmare is included and is non-canon.

editions.name: Red Dead Redemption
editions.note: Original release; Undead Nightmare arrived later as paid DLC.

editions.name: Undead Nightmare Collection
editions.note: Standalone disc of the DLC packs; does not include the main story.

editions.name: Game of the Year Edition
editions.note: Base game plus Undead Nightmare and the multiplayer packs on one disc.

editions.name: Red Dead Redemption (current-gen version)

name: Max Payne
scope: All three. Nothing else in the series exists.
caveat: Chronology and play order agree — three games, in order, no branches, no flashback structure that moves anything.

games.title: Max Payne
games.note: Needs community patches for widescreen and frame pacing on modern displays. Remedy is remaking 1 and 2 as a single title — announced 2022, still unreleased as of August 2026.

editions.name: Max Payne
editions.note: Original release and still the most complete, easiest version to run.

editions.name: Max Payne Mobile
editions.note: Touch port of the full game; controls are the obvious compromise.

games.title: Max Payne 2: The Fall of Max Payne
games.note: Shorter and tighter than the first. Same caveats about modern displays.

games.title: Max Payne 3
games.note: Rockstar-developed, nine years later, São Paulo instead of New York. Requires the Rockstar launcher. Tonally a different game; still the same man.

editions.name: Max Payne 3
editions.note: Base game; DLC packs sold separately through the Rockstar Pass.

editions.name: Complete Edition
editions.note: Bundles every DLC pack; the single-player story itself is unchanged.

name: God of War
scope: Greek saga through Norse saga, handhelds included. Betrayal (2007, mobile) is excluded.
caveat: Ascension is chronologically first and was released second-to-last — it is also the weakest entry, and starting there is the standard mistake. Recommended play order is God of War (2005) → II → III, with the handhelds slotted where they sit, then the 2018 reboot. On PC only the two Norse games exist, and the 2018 game is written to work cold.

games.title: God of War: Ascension
games.note: Set shortly after Kratos breaks his oath to Ares. Prequel, weakest entry, and the wrong place to start. PS3 only — no PS4 or PS5 re-release.

editions.name: God of War: Ascension
editions.note: Only release; never remastered or collected.

editions.name: God of War: Ascension Collector's Edition
editions.note: Statue and art extras; identical game content.

games.title: God of War: Chains of Olympus
games.note: PSP entry, remastered in the PS3 Origins Collection. Sits directly before the 2005 game.

editions.name: God of War: Origins Collection
editions.note: HD remaster paired with Chains of Olympus.

editions.name: God of War Saga

name: The Last of Us
scope: Part I, Left Behind, Part II. The HBO series is not a game and is not tracked.
caveat: Left Behind splits across the timeline — its Riley chapters precede Part I, its Ellie chapters sit inside Part I’s winter section. It is listed after Part I because that is where its framing puts you, and because playing it first spoils Part I’s third act.

name: Halo
scope: Mainline plus Reach and ODST. No Halo Wars, no Spartan Assault, no multiplayer-only releases.
caveat: Reach is a prequel that sorts first and also works as an entry point — a rare case where chronology and a good first game agree. ODST runs concurrently with Halo 2’s Earth arc rather than after it. The real problem with this tab is Halo 5: it has never released on PC and is not in the Master Chief Collection, so a PC-only playthrough has a hole in it right before Infinite.

games.title: Halo: Reach
games.note: August 2552, days before Combat Evolved. The $39.99 buys the whole Master Chief Collection (six campaigns); Reach is also sold on its own for much less.

name: Batman: Arkham
scope: The four mainline Rocksteady and WB Montréal games. No Blackgate, Arkham VR, Shadow, or Suicide Squad.
caveat: Origins is a prequel released third, and it is the one entry where chronology and play order genuinely disagree. It leans on relationships that Asylum and City establish and lands flat as a first game. Recommended play order is Asylum → City → Origins → Knight, or simply Asylum → City → Knight with Origins dropped.

games.title: Batman: Arkham Origins
games.note: Different studio (WB Games Montréal). Chronologically first, but written for players who already know the others. Multiplayer servers are long dead and some save-corruption bugs were never fixed.
